People who earn have the power to decide; we are unemployed and therefore no one in the family will listen to us
Sons get the power of decision making after their father’s death
They (fathers) have more experience than us and so in a better position to take decisions
Lack of education is also a big factor

But education does not guarantee a good job; some well-educated youths are also doing agriculture like their father; there are hardly any good job opportunities here in our village and migrating for work is not always easy
Those who are single can take their decisions
Many parents send their children to school for the free mid-day meal
Children’s education depends on the financial wherewithal of the family
We can purchase a degree if we have the money (for bribing)
We can take decisions pertaining to our education but our freedom to take decisions depends upon how well we do at our exams
I take some decisions since my parents think I am capable enough
If we want to buy something like clothes then we have to take our parent’s permission
Everyone parent wants his children to be educated
Education make us aware of so many things

Getting a good job is very important; one may be just 12th pass but if he has a good government job then he will be well respected and get a good wife but if has a college degree but no job then he will looked upon as a useless fellow
The final aim is to get a good job and education is necessary for that
Life is incomplete without good knowledge
Because I am educated so I know that this a recorder that you are using but an uneducated person would have mistook it for a mobile
Boys study till 10th while girls study till 12th.
Both should be allowed to complete their graduation and also get a technical degree
Technical degree helps in getting a good job
Both will get a good spouse if they are well educated and have a good job
There will be no problem in a girl’s marriage if she is a working woman
Girls’ education is as important as boys’
Education does not bring respect; a good job and a good salary does
But educating a girl does not imply that we will have to pay less dowry since she will want a groom who is as much if not more educated which is possible only if parents give a big dowry
No, parents are partial to their sons when it comes on spending on their education
There are some who are equally dedicated; things are getting better now

Earlier parents had limited money which they preferred to spend on their sons’ education; but now more parents have started sending girls to school; actually elementary education is free for all and parents have realized that girls also have a right to education
But government schools lack qualified teachers
If you ask a graduate the spelling of ten 20% of them will be unable to give the correct answer
Parents who are economically sound are equally committed
The fee at government schools is less but there are fewer seats whereas private colleges demand donations; so education is expensive
Most of them know all agricultural activities
Those who own tractors prepare their fields as well
Some just loiter around and behave like goondas
Most of us know all agricultural activities

Reasons for ending education
• Poor economic condition of the household
• Students are not interested in studies anymore; they are more inclined to dance and cricket
• Some are also under parental pressure to quit studies and start earning
• Peer group effect is also a big reason for students dropping out
• Lack of qualified teachers at school
• Not everyone can pay huge donations at private schools and the government schools which charge less have very few seats

Two most important reasons
• Poor economic condition
• Lack of interest in studies
1. Poor economic condition of the household
2. Lack of interest in studies
Teachers are not qualified which also forces parents to ask their kids to drop out
Who will guide what to study and with what goal in mind?
People decide their career ambition influenced by what they see in movies for example if I like the role of inspector in a movie then I will want to become an inspector
Today we are forced to study and learn everything by rote but we don’t know our career goal yet
There is no one to guide us on a good career path
I would love to go abroad
I wanted to work in a bank but failed the entrance exam
They play cards
Some have set up a mobile repair shop
Some are doing agricultural activities
Some have set up egg and chicken shop
Some have set up musical orchestra
To start a business we need money
Some have got a job too
Everyone should have an aim in life but for that one needs exposure, awareness and proper guidance in the absence of which we just waste away our life
One can become a singer and dancer
One should do a government/private job
One can set up a business

New practices or technologies or information/knowledge
• Rotavator
• Combine
• Cultivator
• Laser land leveler
• Hybrid seeds like 343 and 502

Most important for the [sex of the FGD] of the community (top 2)
• Cultivator
• Combine

Most important for the [opposite sex of FGD] of the community (top 2)
• Women don’t use machines
Two most important for men
Cultivator
Combine
Both the machines save a lot of time for the men
Time and physical effort both
They enable farmers to save on labor cost too
Cultivator digs soil and loosens it properly without much effort

Let us assume that the weather is going to turn bad for the our crop which is ready for harvesting; then a combine can quickly do the work and prevent crop damage whereas if we did it manually we would have definitely lost some portion of our crop
Women don’t use machines
No, women don’t have the same opportunities as men to learn new practices/methods/technologies
The women of our village hardly go anywhere
And women who do engage in farming activities do not have their own land and so they don’t learn new things; they basically work as farm labor
Society has given very little freedom to women

• Zero tiller

• Combine

Information dissemination has become better and people come to our village to educate us
Now income levels have also improved and some people can afford to buy new machines while many others can afford to use them on rent
Now we get lot of information on television and mobile phones too
Yes, men and women have different roles to play in agriculture
Men usually do everything except weeding which is almost always done by women
Men prepare their land, buy all the inputs like seeds, fertilizers etc
Roughly 10% men are involved in sowing
Some men also do harvesting
Women do sowing, weeding and harvesting
They also sort their harvest and prepare it for storage
Girls can never do it alone; they will need help
They will not get their parent’s permission to do something like this
Some men may succeed while others may find it difficult
We know all agricultural activities and are capable enough but we will need a little guidance from our fathers
We can sell by ourselves at government rate
It will not be easy for them either
We can do with help from our fathers
“jisko jisme man lagta hai” i.e. family members can choose whatever they like to do
Women don’t have land of their own
Some men these days are purchasing land in their wives’ name
Husband and wife help each other
If they have had a fight then they will not help and they will hire labor instead
If someone says something bad about such a couple then the man will not hesitate in abusing him
Family members usually help each other
It all depends on family dynamics and relationships; if the family atmosphere is healthy and they all share good rapport then they will not hesitate in helping on both men’s and women’s plots.
Yes, she will consult other farmers
She will first consult her husband and other elders in the family
Husband will also discuss with his wife
He will ask bigger farmers and other elders in the family
People from lower caste will allow their wives to join and even help them in their work
It depends upon the husband
Society norms do not allow women such freedom
He will not allow her to go

This is a tricky scenario since if the husband allows her to go then she will turn around and say “did I marry you and come here to sell vegetables”; so what I am trying to say is that Ana will herself not want to sell
Only a drunk husband will send his wife to sell vegetables
Only women lower caste with very poor economic condition will go to sell vegetables
Women from lower castes but relatively better economic condition will never go
Upper caste women will never want to go
Yes, he will seek less help from Ana now
He will understand that she is very busy now
If she is going to sell in a group then her reputation will not be harmed
If she is a poor women then she will earn people’s respect for working hard for the sake of her family
People’s reaction will depend on the economic condition and need of the family
People will call him names like “nikamma” (good for nothing) and “maugha” (feminine) etc
His friends will laugh at him and make fun of him
People will say he is doing “aiyaashi” (enjoying) and drinking off his wife’s income
No one in the community will like him and they will all avoid him
If he was working and earning then people would not have bothered if his wife also worked but this is a peculiar case and people will definitely talk about it
If she is successful and is giving her earnings to her husband then he will be all praises for her but if she keeps it all to herself then he will fight with her
He will be happy since success implies more money
Gender equality implies similar opportunities in education and job for both the sexes
Government has launched several schemes to ensure gender equality but it will be many ages before we can achieve it
For example women cannot go to work at night unlike men; women’s safety will be threatened
It is not possible to ensure equality in every field
But they should both have equal decision making power
Equality in a sense also implies that if I can beat my wife then she can do likewise too
Women should be able to move around freely
Women should not join police force since that is a man’s profession. Women in police force at Azamgarh are facing a lot of problems

We have to change the mind set of people first if we want to ensure gender equality in our society; we have grown up watching our fathers go for job while our mothers cook at home; this deeply embedded thought process needs to change

If you want to change the society then you have to change the text books taught at school and let children learn that women can also work and men can cook food; only then will we have equality in our society
Both will take joint decision
Men listen to their wives since wives know best how much they need to keep for their family
David will go since women don’t go to sell in the market
Selling is almost invariably a man’s work
Yes, David will take her suggestion and they will make the changes
Since the change is supposed to enhance their production therefore David will be happy to make these changes
The ultimate aim is to increase their income to benefit their family and therefore they will definitely make these changes

Wife can always take a rigid stand to buy land since it is her father’s money

Everything is easy for men given the social settings in which women always have to fight for their rights
He will take the money, buy the bike and start enjoying riding it unbothered about how his wife feels
If his wife fights too much then he will threaten her that he will consume poison f she doesn’t allow him to buy the bike
Women can freely during the day time but after dark they have to stay indoors
During the day there are no security threats
Yes, young women can walk alone comfortably to the local market
Going to the local market is safe during the day
New brides don’t go out in the beginning
And for a long time they have to go accompanied by their husband or some other family member
According to the social customs new brides are the pride of their family and they have to follow all rules to preserve the dignity of the family
But a few years later when she knows everyone and everyone knows her, when she has lived long enough in the community, then she can also move around freely
No women don’t sell in the market
They don’t need to sell; it is their husband’s job
Market is dominated by men and women have no place there

They cannot move alone at night since men get drunk at night and may harass them
But if she is physically strong enough to empower them then she can go at night too
My wife goes alone at night if she has some work at a neighbor’s or friend’s and she has not faced any problem yet
Around 80% young men are migrating to different states in search of better job opportunities
But its note easy to get a job unless we know someone at a good position
A bad contractor will get work done but not pay him
It is never easy in a new place unless we have a relative to help us
If someone has been away for a short while and then returns, his family will not accept him and chase him away; they will ask him to try harder
If a person comes back with money then he can set up a business to benefit the community
Recently a young man went to the city to get a job; he wasted about Rs. 1 lac and returned empty handed; his family was so disappointed because they had pinned all their hopes on him
Girls get married at 18 and boys at 21
Parents take marriage decisions
Sometimes they consult their boys but girls are never asked
Close relatives also participate in this decision making
1%-2% youth have also had love marriage
There is nothing wrong with this system
Parents are experienced enough to decide for us
But they should consult us; girls should also be consulted
This is about lives and we should have some say in it
Marriage decisions depend on dowry; how much a grooms’ father wants and how much a bride’s father can afford to give; no marriage will happen without dowry
At 22-23 years of age
No, women should wait till they are 25 to have their first child
She should be mature enough to raise kids
If she does not conceive within 5 years of marriage then she will herself run away and remarry
Even neighbors and others in the community will start talking that there must be a problem if she has not been able to conceive for so long
25 is the right age
23 is also ok since by then she would have adjusted with her husband and new family
Yes, women can take decision regarding how many children she wants
This is a private matter of the couple and they should discuss and decide
But in Muslim community women have no powers and this decision depends upon the husband
We want job opportunities here in our village
And well-paying jobs
Everyone should learn English
We want good life and good future
